name: Compression Streams
plain: Compresses or decompresses data in the page with built-in gzip, deflate or deflate-raw.
meaning: A site can shrink or expand data without a library. It also lets trackers pack fingerprint payloads before sending them out.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: No iframe flag; available in workers

limits.headline: Can squeeze or unpack data in the page with the browser's built in compression
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a site's script compresses logs, files or data
can: Compress data with gzip or deflate before sending it
Unpack compressed files in the page
Shrink payloads, including tracking data, before they go out
cannot: See your files unless you chose them
Send anything by itself, only change data the page already has
Be turned off from your browser settings
Do heavy work forever, since large tricks can hit memory limits

story.what_it_is: A page can squeeze or unpack data with built in compression, so it sends less over the network.

marketing.name: Compression Streams API
marketing.pitch: Gives pages fast built in gzip and deflate, with no extra code to download.

story.for_you: You never see it. Pages that use it send smaller uploads and open big files faster. It saves time and data.
story.for_makers: Makers drop heavy compression libraries and ship less code. It speeds up uploads, saves and downloads. The same trick can hide the size of data a script sends out, which tracking code can use.

use_cases.example: A browser game compresses save files before uploading them to the cloud, so saves are quick on mobile data.
A web editor compresses documents before sync and saves bandwidth.
A web design tool unpacks large project files in the browser.
A web video app packs frames or clips before an upload.
An analytics script compresses batches of events before sending them in one request.
A web tool lets you drag in a zip or gzip file and view its contents in the page.
A tracking script packs a large fingerprint into a small request that is hard to spot.

technical_bounds: Formats: gzip, deflate, deflate-raw (brotli not in the spec baseline)
Streaming only, no password or zip container; browser does not compress files on disk
DecompressionStream has no output cap; zip bomb risk fills memory

abuse: Memory exhaustion with a decompression bomb
